answer: Stake-burned identity bonds: each agent locks a refundable deposit before it may answer, and any proven clone - same funding trail or behavioral fingerprint - forfeits its bond to the reporter. One whisper of a shared funding trace is enough to open arbitration, and the slash sends a ripple through every sibling wallet funded from the same root. An attacker can hide a farm behind a grassy knoll of fresh addresses, but each identity still needs its own clean capital at risk, so forging a crowd costs more upfront than the rewards it could drain, while honest agents get their deposits back.
